## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Main House
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
**CRITICAL ISSUE IDENTIFIED.** The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a confirmed failure condition requiring immediate professional attention. The pump motor is at risk of overheating without fluid cooling.

All other measured components are in good condition. The tank is sound, the effluent filter is clean, and the dispersal field shows no surface breakout.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT
| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | Baffles intact, no visible damage |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated; soiling light |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 HP, 115V) | **CRITICAL** | Amp draw 1.6A / nameplate 7.2A = 22.2% FLA. No load detected. |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and responding |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry, no ponding or breakout |

## PUMP DIAGNOSTIC
The effluent pump ran during this maintenance visit but drew only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load is a **CRITICAL** condition indicating the pump is running without hydraulic load.

The most likely causes are:
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Dry-run condition (no fluid in pump chamber)

A pump running without load generates heat that the fluid normally dissipates. Continued operation risks motor burnout and complete system failure.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (CRITICAL):**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection or breakage, check the impeller for damage or absence, and verify that fluid is reaching the pump chamber. Do not continue operating the pump until the no-load condition is resolved.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump issue is resolved.
- The tank solids content is within normal range. Routine pumping is not required at this time, but monitor at the next maintenance visit.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your system uses an aerobic treatment unit, which requires an effluent pump to move treated water from the tank to the dispersal field. During this maintenance visit, the pump was running but drawing almost no electrical current -- a sign that it is not moving water.

This can happen if the pump's discharge line has come loose or cracked, if the impeller inside the pump has broken, or if the pump is running dry. In any case, the pump cannot do its job and the system cannot disperse treated effluent. The motor is also at risk of damage from overheating.

**Do not delay.** Contact a qualified technician to examine the pump and discharge line and restore normal operation.

### Managing Solids
Your tank solids measured 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time as bacteria break down waste. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable. The tank will require pumping when solids reach about 33 percent of volume, typically every 3 to 5 years depending on household size and water use.
